item.title: Pbd Podcast Debate: Owens, Wilson clash over Kirk killing; proof of Israeli role still missing
item.description: Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson debated claims about Charlie Kirk’s killing on the PBD Podcast. Wilson is a Christian conservative commentator known for The Crucible and Debate University. Owens did not prove that Israel was directly involved in Kirk’s killing. The debate drew more than 3.1 million views in under 24 hours, while the $500,000 payment remained unclear.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Mahomes Ranking Backlash: Dan Orlovsky’s QB trait list irks Chiefs fans; trainer vows to ‘keep Dan informed’
item.description: Patrick Mahomes has found himself at the center of a fresh NFL debate after Dan Orlovsky ranked him outside the top 10 in several quarterback traits, including ball placement, mechanics and pocket presence. Mahomes’ longtime trainer Bobby Stroupe responded pointedly, writing, “Oh. �� We will keep Dan informed as the season goes on.” Chiefs fans quickly rallied behind Mahomes, expecting the recovering superstar to answer his critics once he returns.

item.title: Streamer Arrest Sparks Probe: Los Angeles police hold Salazar; attempted murder allegation remains
item.description: Kick streamer and TikTok creator Santos Salazar was arrested in Los Angeles following a reported domestic violence incident and is facing an attempted murder allegation. His bail was reportedly set at $1 million. Salazar and partner Brianna Olsen recently welcomed their son, Sunday Ray, and shared family updates online. Olsen later posted footage appearing to show Salazar’s arrest and said she had been speaking with lawyers. The investigation remains ongoing.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Debate Over Kirk Evidence: Owens’ theories face scrutiny on PBD Podcast; Wilson demands proof
item.description: Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson faced off in a heated debate over the death of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. Owens questioned aspects of the official account and raised theories involving possible foreign involvement, while Wilson challenged her to provide evidence. The discussion also turned personal after Wilson accused Owens of using her phone for answers. Moderator Patrick Bet-David refused to declare a winner, saying, “The people won today.”
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Hungary bus crash: 12 killed, 10 injured after Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway
item.description: Twelve people died and ten were seriously injured after a Polish bus overturned early Sunday. The bus ran off the M3 motorway and tipped into a ditch near Mezokeresztes. Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced the tragic casualties on Facebook. He also expressed his sincere condolences to the families of the victims. The exact cause of the accident remains unknown at this time.

item.title: ‘Always proud’: Kim Jong Un hails Russia ties in message to Putin
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and Russian President Vladimir Putin have reaffirmed their close relationship. Their countries are actively cooperating in all sectors, ensuring regional security and stability. This growing partnership has deepened significantly since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. North Korea has provided troops and weapons to support Moscow's war effort. This exchange highlights competing diplomatic and security dynamics on the Korean peninsula.

item.title: Qatar calls Iran’s claim ‘misleading’, denies capturing 3 pilots after March strike
item.description: Qatar denied Iran's claims about holding three captured military pilots. Iranian jets allegedly violated Qatari airspace during a March operation. Qatar stated it found remains of one pilot and attempted contact. Authorities defended their territory after receiving no response from the pilots. The denial comes amid regional efforts to ease tensions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why Hurricane Lala is a historic threat to Hawaii’s Big Island
item.description: Hurricane Lala approached Hawaii's Big Island as a Category 1 storm. Powerful winds and heavy rain brought dangerous surf and potential flooding. Over 40,000 utility customers across Hawaii lost electricity. Residents prepared for destructive winds, falling trees, and extended power outages. The storm's path raised concerns about mudslides and wildfires.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 19th-century ships accidentally brought mice to islands 30 miles off San Francisco
item.description: The Farallon Islands are grappling with an overwhelming invasion of house mice, significantly disturbing the delicate ecological system. These rodents threaten the survival of native wildlife, with burrowing owls preying on them and subsequently impacting the vulnerable Ashy storm-petrels. A new eradication initiative involves dropping rodenticide bait from helicopters, driving efforts to restore the natural balance of this unique ecosystem.

item.title: In 1987, a British naturalist became the first professional warden of a remote Seychelles island
item.description: In 1987, British naturalist Ian Bullock established Aride Island as a key conservation hub. His initiative led to the successful relocation of endangered Seychelles warblers the following year, significantly bolstering the species' numbers and preventing potential extinction. Today, their population thrives, and Bullock's innovative conservation methods are now standard practices in island ecosystem management.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2023, Chris Pratt listed his Pacific Palisades mansion for $32 million; three years later...
item.description: After multiple price adjustments and relisting efforts, Chris Pratt and Katherine Schwarzenegger are once again offering their Pacific Palisades home for $19.99 million. Originally bought for $15.6 million in 2018, this marks their fifth try to sell the opulent estate, which boasts six bedroom suites along with ample outdoor living spaces, a true testament to luxury living in Los Angeles.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2011, Myanmar suspended a giant China-backed dam after public outrage; it now plans to...
item.description: Myanmar has announced plans to resume the Myitsone hydropower project, valued at $3.6 billion, which has been inactive for 14 years. This China-supported initiative aims to provide essential electricity to the nation. However, challenges regarding environmental degradation and potential displacement for local communities raise serious concerns. Additionally, fears of earthquakes add a layer of safety apprehension for populations living downstream.

item.title: Meet Jamie Bell, 18-year-old London teen who started selling old Lego at 13 and generated over...
item.description: Eighteen-year-old Jamie Bell has remarkably transformed his Lego reselling passion into JTB Collectables, a burgeoning enterprise generating upwards of four hundred thousand dollars annually. Specializing in bulk Lego lots and sought-after minifigures, he appeals to other collectors. As he prepares for university, Jamie aims to grow his business further, securing his financial footing and building savings for the years ahead.
